Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the call this morning. A couple of follow-up questions from our security and infra teams so we can prepare the internal briefing: 

1) Region pinning: can Redwood pin a tenant's data and inference workloads to a single region (US-EAST) and prevent any PII or model input/output from leaving that region? What happens with cross-region failover — is data replicated across regions automatically or only on request?

2) Backups & recovery: where are persistent backups stored by default, and can backups be constrained to the same region? What's the RPO/RTO for a cross-region failover scenario?

3) Logging/audit: what logs (request payloads, system logs, access logs) are stored and for how long by default? Can we configure retention/purge windows and provide evidence for audits (S3 links or syslog exports)?

4) KMS / encryption: do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) and can we specify the KMS region for key storage?

5) PII handling: are there built-in controls to avoid storing user-provided PII in persistent stores (e.g., configurable input redaction or disabling persistent KV caching)?

If you have a short one-pager or diagram that explains the regional failover behavior and where backups/logs live, that would be super helpful for the security review.

Also looping Tom (infra) — Tom, any additional items you'd like us to push on?

Thanks,

Hi Priya —

Great questions — thanks for outlining them so clearly. Summary answers below, and attaching a short whitepaper + a high-level data flow diagram that show the default behaviour and options. Aditya & Marissa are cc'd for technical and procurement next steps.

Quick answers (high-level):
- Region pinning: Yes. We can pin a customer's control plane and data plane to a single region (e.g., us-east-1). When region-pinning is enabled, inference requests, model KV caches, persistent storage, and backups remain in the selected region by default.
- Cross-region failover: Not automatic by default. We support two patterns: 1) Primary-only: no replication — fastest, no cross-region copies; 2) Primary + warm-standby: asynchronous replication to a configured secondary region (for failover). Warm-standby requires explicit enablement and has additional configuration and contractual requirements.
- Backups: Snapshots are stored in the pinned region by default. For warm-standby setups we replicate encrypted snapshots to the standby region; replication is asynchronous (near-real-time depending on snapshot cadence). RPO/RTO depends on snapshot frequency and bootstrap time — typical default snapshot cadence is nightly (RPO ~24h) with failover time measured in minutes-to-hours depending on model weights and cache warmup. We can discuss tighter RPOs for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Logging & audit: Access logs (who/when), system logs, and aggregated usage metrics are stored in-region by default. Raw request payload retention is configurable — default retention is 30 days; enterprise plans can extend to 365 days or export to customer-owned logging sinks. We support S3 delivery or syslog/forwarders for audit evidence.
- KMS/Encryption: We support customer-managed keys (CMK). Customers can supply a KMS key and specify the KMS region for key storage. All backups and persisted stores can be encrypted with CMK if requested.
- PII controls: Persistent KV caching and prefix caching are configurable per-customer and can be disabled. We also support automated redaction pipelines (configurable) to remove PII before persistence.

3) Marissa will follow up with procurement items and an initial pilot SOW for a pinned-region proof-of-concept.

Hi Priya / Tom —

A few technical clarifications from the runtime side to supplement Laura's note:

- KV / cache: The serving runtime keeps KV caches and intermediate token caches on the serving nodes. These caches are ephemeral by design — they are not written to long-term persistent stores unless you enable a persistent cache feature. If you need zero persistence of model inputs/outputs, we can disable persistent caching for the tenant.

- Input storage: Model inputs are by default processed in-memory; we only persist inputs if you enable features that require persistence (e.g., long-term evaluation, audit logging of raw requests). Those persistence sinks live in-region when region-pinning is enabled.

- Backups / replication details: Our standard backup cadence is once per 24 hours (snapshot of model artifacts + metadata). For warm-standby replication we stream encrypted snapshots to the secondary region; this is asynchronous. If you require a sub-24h RPO, we can support increased snapshot frequency or continuous replication in Dedicated setups (requires additional provisioning).

- RTO: Failover time depends on the artifact size and cache warmup. For typical model artifacts we expect RTO in the order of 30-90 minutes for a warm-standby; cold failover from nothing will take longer. We can provide a runbook and timing estimates after we know model sizes and concurrency targets.

- KMS specifics: We integrate with major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). If you provide a CMK, we will only reference encryption keys in the specified region and will not export keys outside that region. Keys remain customer-managed; Redwood never has access to plaintext keys.

- Logs / export: We can deliver structured request logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket in your account (in-region). Alternately we support streaming to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder.

Happy to jump on a 20-30 minute technical call to walk through a sample architecture for Acme's environment. Laura / Marissa — please let me know when you'd like me on.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
